name: semantic-crosscheck
description: Cross-layer verification for an ontology plus semantic layer on PostgreSQL 17, for Codex and Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Prove that a PostgreSQL closure, SHACL rules, OWL reasoning and a Cube model agree.
interface.longDescription: Release v0.9.0: cross-checks PostgreSQL 17 closures, SQL and SHACL rules, OWL/HermiT and Cube against gold SQL. Adds an optional expect stage that runs the gold SQL and Cube on a user-loaded dedicated fixture database with explicit consent and compares both with literal expected rows written from the business specification, so a mistake the gold SQL and the configuration share fails as common_mode. V3 pair tests can compare every key in chunks up to verify.pair_key_budget and count the keys Cube answered, and shacl-corpus --w3c-suite checks pySHACL and Apache Jena against the pinned W3C SHACL core suite inside the sxc profile. Keys missing from a chunked pair test's Cube answers, changed fixtures, unpinned suites and missing engines cannot pass (sampled pair tests do not yet check answered keys); expect results stay outside report and V1-V5 coverage. Existing configurations and defaults remain supported. Rerun build, reason, cube, verify and report after upgrading; no shared MVCC snapshot or runtime attestation is claimed.
defaultPrompt: Use semantic-crosscheck to run the synthetic demo end to end.
Use semantic-crosscheck to verify my crosscheck.toml against PostgreSQL and explain what is not proven.
